0.0.n: A conversational opener here, rather than an answer meaning yes.

0.2.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery.

0.4.n: Part of the English channel name, not a separate Japanese word.

0.6.n: Completes the English name The Game Gallery.

0.8.n: An English loanword written in katakana.

0.9.n: Links the channel to Haru99, indicating affiliation.

0.10.n: The name portion of the speaker’s username Haru99.

0.11.n: These digits are part of the username Haru99, not a quantity.

0.12.n: A polite sentence ending; the speaker leaves I unstated.

1.0.n: Sets the time for the introduction.

1.1.n: Adds a friendly pause and draws the listener’s attention.

1.3.n: 紹介する means to introduce; ご adds respect toward the audience.

1.4.n: Turns ご紹介する into a noun-like phrase: what I will introduce.

1.5.n: Marks what the speaker will introduce as the topic.

1.7.n: Indicates that the item is visible before the speaker names it.

1.8.n: Points to the place where the item is visible.

1.9.n: Marks the location where something appears.

1.10.n: Short for 出ています, describing something currently visible.

1.11.n: Softly connects this aside to the introduction that follows.

2.1.n: The first part of the game title ネットランナー, Netrunner.

2.2.n: The second part of the game title, not a person running here.

2.4.n: Links the game title to its Japanese edition.

2.5.n: Combines 日本語, Japanese language, with 版, edition.

2.6.n: Politely identifies the item introduced in the previous line.

2.7.n: Makes the identification conversational and invites shared attention.

3.0.n: The first part of the game title Netrunner.

3.1.n: Completes the game title ネットランナー.

3.2.n: Pairs with いえば to form といえば, meaning speaking of.

3.3.n: The conditional form of いう; といえば introduces something associated with the topic.

3.5.n: Combines with 前 to describe an unspecified time in the past.

3.6.n: Follows a duration to place it before the present.

3.7.n: Marks しばらく前 as the time of the earlier introduction.

3.8.n: Directly modifies 体験版, pointing to a particular demo version.

3.9.n: Refers to a version designed for trying the game.

3.10.n: Part of a polite aside identifying the demo before the speaker continues.

3.11.n: Invites the listener to recognize the demo being mentioned.

4.0.n: Modifies デッキ to specify a deck for trying the game.

4.1.n: A katakana loanword referring to a set of game cards.

4.2.n: Links the demo deck to its contents.

4.3.n: Refers to what is included inside the demo deck.

4.4.n: Marks 中身 as the thing the speaker previously introduced.

4.6.n: The respectful prefix ご combines with いたしました to politely describe the speaker’s action.

4.7.n: The polite past form of いたす, a humble alternative to する.

4.8.n: Connects the earlier demo introduction to the contrast with the commercial version.

5.0.n: A polite way to point to the version being discussed.

5.1.n: Connects こちら to 製品版, making it this commercial version.

5.2.n: Contrasts the product sold to customers with the demo version.

5.4.n: Marks the commercial version as the topic, contrasting it with the demo.

5.5.n: Used with a negative verb to describe something not done by that point.

5.6.n: Adds a conversational pause without changing the main statement.

5.8.n: Strengthens the negative statement that no review had been done.

5.9.n: レビューする plus ていませんでした gives a polite past negative, describing what had not been done.

5.10.n: Gives the lack of a previous review as the reason for the current one.

6.0.n: Sets the current occasion apart from the earlier demo introduction.

6.1.n: Signals the first step or item in the planned coverage.

6.3.n: Points to the particular Japanese edition being presented.

6.4.n: The first part of the game title Netrunner.

6.5.n: Completes the game title ネットランナー.

6.6.n: Follows the game title directly to identify its language edition.

6.7.n: Links the Japanese edition to the unboxing review.

6.8.n: Literally opening a sealed package; it modifies レビュー here.

6.9.n: An English loanword used as a noun here.

6.10.n: Politely states what this installment will cover.

6.11.n: Softens the announcement and keeps the tone conversational.

0.lit: Yes, [I] am Haru99 of The Game Gallery channel.
0.tip: The pattern organization の name です is a common way to introduce yourself with your affiliation.

1.lit: Today, you know, what [I] will introduce is already showing here, though...
1.tip: A verb followed by のは sets up what the speaker will identify next.

2.lit: [It] is the Japanese edition of Netrunner, you see.
2.tip: This line completes the what I will introduce topic from the previous line.

3.lit: Speaking of Netrunner, a while ago, this demo version, you see...
3.tip: といえば means speaking of and introduces a related memory or topic.

4.lit: [I] once humbly introduced the contents of the demo deck, but...
4.tip: ご紹介いたしました is a humble, polite way to say that you introduced something.

5.lit: As for this commercial version, [I] had not reviewed [it] at all yet, you know, so...
5.tip: まだ with a negative means not yet; ので connects that situation to the reason for today’s review.

6.lit: This time, first, [it] is an unboxing review of this Netrunner Japanese edition, you see.
6.tip: 開封レビュー combines opening the package with reviewing what is inside.
